findings.statement: A compact asymmetric local-recovery equation predicts future released population-trace means across held animals better than registered controls in mean error

reliability.rationale: Selected asymmetric recovery MAE0.000276179 improves persistence0.000336935 and flexible0.000303232 across five held animals. Selection remains006 although004 has marginally lower exposed confirmation error.

mechanism.rationale: Local recovery and asymmetric increments are interpretable descriptions of the processed signal. Undocumented normalization, component-exclusion flags and upstream smoothing prevent identification of calcium lifetime, spike rate, coupling or fear mechanism.

novelty.rationale: Autoregressive/relaxation models and the source hippocampal fear/context result are prior art. No exhaustive novelty or new neural law is established.

significance.rationale: Useful source-component forecasting reference with whole-animal transfer and explicit rejection of ambiguous behavior-aligned endpoints; practical amplitude meaning is unresolved.

reproducibility.rationale: Native frame-index extraction, source anchors, frozen coefficients, allowed prefixes, sample/group contracts and complete attempt comparisons inspected; separate computational replay is assigned to root.

impact.rationale: No behavior prediction, treatment effect, clinical outcome or deployed device benefit was measured.

reliability.rationale: All saved predictions and primary metrics independently reproduce from source-verified inputs, including unfavorable alternatives. An asymmetric recovery predictor improves processed-calcium trace forecasting on five held animals, with all sessions linked. Units remain author trace units and time is native frames; behavior-only files and unresolved freezing alignment are excluded. No neural/fear mechanism, spike rate or quality-flag interpretation is invented.
